userStories.title: Context Extraction API — multi-mode LLM-powered YAML generation
userStories.description:
Backend API that accepts context from six different input modes and uses the LLM to extract structured Direction Stack YAML. This is the engine behind the Bootstrap Context Modal (U-008).

File: ~/rorcha/backend/src/routes/context.ts
File: ~/rorcha/backend/src/lib/context-extractor.ts

Install multer for file uploads:
```bash
cd ~/rorcha/backend && npm install multer @types/multer
```

---

**Shared extraction interface:**
```typescript
export interface ExtractionResult {
  yaml: string;                 // The generated YAML string
  confidence: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low';  // LLM self-assessment
  extracted: string[];          // Fields successfully extracted, e.g. ['project.purpose', 'project.stack']
  missing: string[];            // Fields LLM flagged as missing/unclear
  rawInput: string;             // The combined text that was sent to the LLM (for transparency)
  tokenCount: number;           // Approximate input token count
}
```

---

**Endpoint 1: POST /api/context/extract**

Content-Type: application/json

Request body is a discriminated union on `mode`:

```typescript
type ExtractRequest =
  | { mode: 'qa';         answers: Record<string, string>; targetLayer: 1|2|3 }
  | { mode: 'paste';      text: string;                    targetLayer: 1|2|3 }
  | { mode: 'filepath';   filePath: string;                targetLayer: 1|2|3 }
  | { mode: 'url';        url: string;                     targetLayer: 1|2|3 }
  | { mode: 'multi';      sources: MultiSource[];          targetLayer: 1|2|3 }

interface MultiSource {
  type: 'paste' | 'filepath' | 'url';
  content: string;   // text for paste, path for filepath, URL for url
  label?: string;    // e.g. 'README', 'Architecture Doc', 'Database Schema'
}
```

Processing per mode:

**`qa` mode:**
- Receives the 9 Q&A answers from the wizard (see U-008 for question list)
- Formats them as a labelled list, sends to LLM with layer-specific extraction prompt
- Example assembled input:
  ```
  Project name: Freelance Invoicing SaaS
  What does it do: Creates invoices, tracks payment, sends Stripe links
  Primary users: Freelancers and their clients
  Tech stack: React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Stripe
  Three key features: Online booking, deposit payments, appointment reminders
  Hard constraints: Offline invoice drafting, no card data storage
  V1 definition of done: Artist takes a booking+deposit without DMs
  Existing codebase: No — greenfield
  Similar products for reference: Wave, FreshBooks (simpler)
  ```

**`paste` mode:**
- Raw text as-is, truncated at 12,000 chars with a warning if exceeded

**`filepath` mode:**
- Backend reads file at absolute path using fs.readFileSync
- Supported file types by extension:
  - `.md` → read as-is (markdown)
  - `.txt` → read as-is
  - `.sql` → extract CREATE TABLE blocks only (strip ALTER, INSERT, etc. — reuse Schema Hydrator logic from H-001)
  - `.prisma` → read as-is (Prisma schema is self-documenting)
  - `.ts` / `.tsx` → extract type definitions and interfaces only (regex: `(export )?(interface|type) \w+`)
  - `.json` → read as-is, pretty-printed
  - `.yaml` / `.yml` → read as-is
  - Other → read first 8000 chars as plain text
- Returns 400 if file doesn't exist or is a directory

**`url` mode:**
- Backend fetches the URL (server-side, avoids CORS)
- User-Agent: 'Rorcha/1.0 context-hydrator'
- Timeout: 10 seconds
- Supported URL patterns with special handling:
  - `github.com/*/blob/*` → rewrite to `raw.githubusercontent.com` and fetch raw text
  - `github.com/*/README*` → fetch via GitHub raw URL
  - Any URL → fetch HTML, strip tags (regex strip `<[^>]+>`, collapse whitespace), keep first 10,000 chars
- Returns 400 if URL is non-public (localhost, 192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x blocked)
- Returns 408 on timeout

**`multi` mode:**
- Processes each source in parallel (Promise.all)
  - `paste` source → use text directly
  - `filepath` source → read file (same logic as filepath mode)
  - `url` source → fetch URL (same logic as url mode)
- Concatenates all source texts with labeled separators:
  ```
  === Source: README ===
  {readme content}

  === Source: Architecture Doc ===
  {arch doc content}

  === Source: Database Schema ===
  {schema content}
  ```
- Total truncated at 16,000 chars (larger budget because user intentionally combined sources)
- Single LLM pass over the combined text — do NOT make one LLM call per source

---

**LLM extraction prompt (in context-extractor.ts):**

```typescript
function buildExtractionPrompt(rawText: string, targetLayer: 1|2|3): string {
  const layerInstructions = {
    1: `You are extracting GLOBAL AI BEHAVIOR guidelines (L1 — Global Brain).
Extract: preferred coding style, output format preferences, things to always/never do,
general persona or tone, global constraints that apply to all projects.
YAML root key: 'global'`,

    2: `You are extracting DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE (L2 — Domain Profile).
Extract: industry/domain concepts, regulatory constraints, business terminology,
domain-specific gotchas, reference architectures common in this domain.
YAML root key: 'domain'`,

    3: `You are extracting PROJECT CONTEXT (L3 — Project Brief).
Extract: project name, what it does (one sentence), primary users, tech stack,
key features (top 3-5), hard constraints, v1 definition of done, integrations,
similar products for reference.
YAML root key: 'project'`,
  };

  return `${layerInstructions[targetLayer]}

Source material:
<source>
${rawText}
</source>

Return ONLY valid YAML. No markdown fences, no explanation before or after.
After the YAML, on a new line starting with '#meta', add a JSON object:
#meta {"confidence":"high|medium|low","extracted":["field1","field2"],"missing":["field3"]}

For confidence:
- high: source clearly states all key fields
- medium: most fields present but some inferred or incomplete
- low: source is vague, tangential, or missing critical fields`;
}
```

Parse the response by splitting on `#meta` — everything before is YAML, everything after is the JSON metadata object.

---

**Endpoint 2: POST /api/context/upload**

Content-Type: multipart/form-data
Fields: `files` (multiple file inputs), `targetLayer` (1|2|3)

- Uses multer with memoryStorage (no disk write — files stay in memory)
- Limit: 10 files max, 5MB per file
- Reads each uploaded file buffer as UTF-8 text
- Combines into multi-source format with `label: originalFilename`
- Then calls the same extraction pipeline as `multi` mode
- Returns ExtractionResult

```typescript
const upload = multer({
  storage: multer.memoryStorage(),
  limits: { fileSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024, files: 10 },
  fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => {
    const allowed = ['.md','.txt','.sql','.prisma','.ts','.tsx','.json','.yaml','.yml','.py','.rb','.go'];
    const ext = path.extname(file.originalname).toLowerCase();
    cb(null, allowed.includes(ext));
  }
});

router.post('/upload', upload.array('files'), async (req, res) => { ... });
```

---

**Endpoint 3: GET /api/context/fetch-preview?url=**

- Proxy endpoint: fetches the URL and returns the first 500 chars as a preview
- Used by the URL tab in U-008 to show a preview before full extraction
- Same URL validation (block private IPs)
- Returns { preview: string, contentLength: number, contentType: string }

---

**File: ~/rorcha/backend/src/routes/__tests__/context.test.ts**

- Test `paste` mode: sends text → mock chatComplete → verifies YAML in response
- Test `qa` mode: sends answers object → verifies answers are assembled into labelled list before LLM call
- Test `filepath` mode: mock fs.readFileSync → verifies file content sent to LLM
- Test `filepath` with .sql extension: verifies only CREATE TABLE blocks extracted
- Test `filepath` with .ts extension: verifies only interface/type declarations extracted
- Test `url` mode: mock fetch → verifies HTML stripped to plain text
- Test `url` mode with github.com/*/blob/* URL: verifies rewrite to raw.githubusercontent.com
- Test `url` mode blocks localhost: returns 400
- Test `multi` mode: mock three sources → verifies combined text has labeled separators
- Test `upload` endpoint: mock multer files → verifies multi-source extraction called
- Test confidence parsing: verifies '#meta' line parsed correctly from LLM response
- Test missing/empty sources: graceful error, not 500

userStories.title: Bootstrap Context Modal — six input methods with preview and accept flow
userStories.description:
The full-featured onboarding modal for populating the Direction Stack from a new project. Accessible from a 'Bootstrap Context' button in the Direction Stack Composer (U-003). Covers every realistic way a user might have project context available: Q&A wizard, paste, single-file upload, multi-file upload, filesystem path, URL fetch. All methods feed into a unified preview → edit → accept flow.

File: ~/rorcha/src/components/BootstrapContextModal.tsx

Trigger: Add a 'Bootstrap Context ✦' button to the layer editor header in DirectionStackPanel (U-003). Position: top-right of the layer editor column, next to the layer tabs.

```typescript
interface BootstrapContextModalProps {
  workspaceId: string;
  activeLayer: 1 | 2 | 3;          // Pre-selects which layer to populate
  onAccept: (yaml: string) => void; // Called when user confirms — updates the layer textarea
  onClose: () => void;
}
```

Modal size: 780px wide, 85vh tall, centered, dark overlay behind.

---

**Modal header:**
```
✦ Bootstrap Context
[Layer selector]: ● L1 Global Brain  ● L2 Domain Profile  ● L3 Project Brief
Close [X]
```
Layer radio group at the top — switches which layer will be populated. Pre-selected to the activeLayer prop.

---

**Tab strip (6 methods):**
```
[🧙 Wizard] [📋 Paste] [📁 Upload] [🗂 File Path] [🔗 URL] [⚡ Multi-Source]
```

---

**Tab 1: Wizard (🧙)**

Step-by-step Q&A. 9 questions displayed one at a time with a progress bar (1/9, 2/9...).
Each question has a text input (or textarea for multi-line answers).
Navigation: [← Back] [Next →] buttons. Skip option on every question.
Final step shows a summary before extraction.

Question list (with placeholders):
```
1. What is the project name?
   placeholder: 'freelance-invoicing'

2. What does it do? (one sentence)
   placeholder: 'Invoicing and payment tracking for freelancers'

3. Who are the primary users?
   placeholder: 'Freelancers and their clients'

4. What is the tech stack? (comma-separated, or 'Not decided yet')
   placeholder: 'React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Stripe'

5. What are the 3 most important features?
   placeholder: 'Online booking, deposit payments, appointment reminders'
   type: textarea (3 rows)

6. What are the hard constraints? (things that must not change)
   placeholder: 'Must work offline, no card data stored on our servers'
   type: textarea (3 rows)

7. What does v1 done look like? (one sentence)
   placeholder: 'An artist can accept a booking + deposit without any back-and-forth DMs'

8. Is this greenfield or an existing codebase?
   type: radio — [Greenfield — new project] [Existing codebase]

9. Any similar products for reference? (helps calibrate UX expectations)
   placeholder: 'Wave, FreshBooks — but simpler and mobile-first'
```

On 'Extract →' (shown at step 9 summary):
- Calls POST /api/context/extract with mode='qa', answers={}, targetLayer
- Shows spinner: 'Extracting context...'
- On success: transitions to Preview pane (see below)

---

**Tab 2: Paste (📋)**

Layout:
```
[Layer: L3 Project Brief ▾]   [Paste text → Extract]

┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Paste any text here — a PRD, whitepaper,│
│ design doc, Notion export, meeting notes│
│ or even a rough brain dump.             │
│                                         │
│ (textarea, 18 rows, resizable)          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘

X / 12,000 chars    [⚠ Truncated at 12,000] (warning when exceeded)

[Extract to YAML →]  (disabled when empty)
```

Calls POST /api/context/extract with mode='paste', text, targetLayer.

---

**Tab 3: Upload (📁)**

File upload supporting multiple files at once.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                              │
│   [  drag files here, or click to browse  ] │
│                                              │
│   Supported: .md .txt .sql .prisma           │
│              .ts .tsx .json .yaml .py .go    │
│   Up to 10 files · 5MB each                 │
│                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Uploaded files:
  ✓ README.md              (4.2 KB)  [✕]
  ✓ schema.sql             (12.1 KB) [✕]
  ✓ architecture.md        (8.6 KB)  [✕]
  ⚠ image.png              Skipped — unsupported type

[Extract All →]   (disabled until ≥1 valid file)

- `<input type="file" multiple accept="..." />` hidden, triggered by drag-drop zone or click
- Files shown in a list with remove buttons
- Unsupported file types shown with warning, not added to the list
- On Extract: POST /api/context/upload with FormData containing all files + targetLayer

---

**Tab 4: File Path (🗂)**

For when the file already exists on the server's filesystem (most common: registered workspace files).

```
Absolute file path:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ /Users/me/my-project/CLAUDE.md                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
[Browse workspace files ▾]   (dropdown listing workspace root + common files)

Quick picks (auto-populated from workspace.path):
  • README.md
  • CLAUDE.md
  • docs/architecture.md
  • backend/src/db/migrations/  (all .sql files → Schema Hydrator)
  ← detected by checking if each file exists via GET /api/workspace/:id/files?patterns=...

[Extract from File →]
```

Backend endpoint for quick picks — GET /api/workspaces/:id/files?patterns=README.md,CLAUDE.md,docs/*.md,**/*.sql
- Returns { exists: string[] } — list of files that actually exist at those paths
- No content returned yet (content is read server-side during extraction)

On Extract: POST /api/context/extract with mode='filepath', filePath, targetLayer.

---

**Tab 5: URL (🔗)**

```
Fetch from URL:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ https://github.com/user/repo/blob/main/README.md    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
[Preview ↗]   (loads GET /api/context/fetch-preview, shows snippet)

Preview (appears after clicking Preview):
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Content-Type: text/plain · ~4,200 chars             │
│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ # My Awesome Project                                │
│ A SaaS for freelancers to manage their invoicing... │
│ (first 500 chars)                                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Tips:
  • GitHub blob URLs are auto-converted to raw content
  • Public Notion pages, docs sites, and wikis work too
  • Private/authenticated URLs will not load

[Extract from URL →]   (disabled until URL entered)
```

On Extract: POST /api/context/extract with mode='url', url, targetLayer.

---

**Tab 6: Multi-Source (⚡)**

The power user tab. Add multiple sources of any type, label them, extract once.

```
⚡ Combine multiple sources into one extraction pass
Each source is read and merged — the LLM sees all content together.

Sources:  [+ Add Source]

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ #1  [Type ▾: File Path]  Label: README        [✕ Remove]   │
│     Path: /Users/me/my-project/README.md                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ #2  [Type ▾: Paste]      Label: Architecture  [✕ Remove]   │
│     ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐              │
│     │ We use PostgreSQL with row-level...    │              │
│     └────────────────────────────────────────┘              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ #3  [Type ▾: URL]        Label: API Docs      [✕ Remove]   │
│     URL: https://docs.stripe.com/api                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Estimated context: ~8,400 chars (of 16,000 max)   [████████░░ 52%]

[Extract All Sources →]
```

State shape:
```typescript
interface MultiSourceEntry {
  id: string;        // uuid for React key
  type: 'paste' | 'filepath' | 'url';
  label: string;
  content: string;   // text for paste, path for filepath, URL for url
}
```

[+ Add Source] adds a new empty entry with type selector dropdown.
Each entry's type selector switches between paste textarea, path input, URL input.
Char count estimates: paste = content.length, filepath/URL = 3000 (estimate until fetched).
Total bar shows aggregate vs 16,000 char budget.

On Extract: POST /api/context/extract with mode='multi', sources=[], targetLayer.

---

**Universal Preview Pane (shown after any extraction):**
